tools.name: ask_maximo
tools.description: Answer a practical IBM Maximo question from Assetize’s published, source-backed knowledge. The answer cites its evidence ([R#] markers with source URLs) and DECLINES when the published record cannot support one — it never guesses. Best for how-to, troubleshooting, version-behaviour and error questio

tools.name: search_records
tools.description: Fast keyword search over published Assetize knowledge records. Returns slugs, titles and short answers with record URLs.

tools.name: lookup_error_code
tools.description: Find published records about a specific Maximo error or fix identifier (BMXAA1234E, IJ12345, APAR...).

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: Fetch one published record by slug: the established fact, claims, version scope, and every cited source URL.

tools.name: compare_maximo_versions
tools.description: Compare two Maximo versions/eras and get a cited upgrade-impact report per functional area: changes to absorb (deprecations, behaviour changes, API changes, gotchas), fixes/APARs since, and newly announced capability — the last two reported as context only, never scored as upgrade work. Same reviewe

tools.name: maximo_changelog
tools.description: The dated, source-cited log of what changed across IBM Maximo / MAS 9.x (9.1 onward): deprecations, behaviour changes, API/fixes, security, gotchas, upgrades, lifecycle and releases. Only real change records (never data-dictionary noise) and nothing the curator demoted. Same data as assetize.com.au/

tools.name: change_watch
tools.description: The curated feed of genuinely material IBM Maximo / MAS 9.x changes — security, upgrades, deprecations, releases, behaviour and migration breaks. Each carries What Changed / Why It Matters, previous behaviour, a version comparison, a clearly-labelled Assetize interpretation (never presented as IBM’s

tools.name: list_gotchas
tools.description: Known traps, upgrade landmines, installation issues, security and troubleshooting records — optionally scoped to a version. Same data as assetize.com.au/gotchas.

tools.name: records_by_version
tools.description: Every published record scoped to a given Maximo version or family (e.g. "9.2", "7.6.1"). Same data as assetize.com.au/maximo/<version>.

tools.name: behaviour_history
tools.description: Historical, lifecycle, behaviour-change, deprecation, architecture and API records — the "how did this get here / when does it end" archaeology. Same data as assetize.com.au/archaeology.

tools.name: support_lifecycle
tools.description: IBM Maximo / MAS support-lifecycle facts: end-of-support / Extended Support transitions and the 2026/2027 deadlines, drawn from source-backed lifecycle records and the curated Change Watch. Optionally scope to a version.

tools.name: corpus_stats
tools.description: Coverage / transparency stats for the Assetize corpus: published records, unique source documents, versions represented, and raw evidence items.

tools.name: test_automation_script_evidence
tools.description: Statically check a WORKORDER Object launch point Automation Script (Jython or JavaScript) against one release lens's real MXAPIWODETAIL dictionary. Extracts every attribute the script references via mbo.getString/setValue/isNull/getInt/getDate/getBoolean, then reports which ones the named lens has e

tools.name: upgrade_plan
tools.description: One Maximo move from an earlier catalogue release to a later one (7.6.1, 8.11, 9.0, 9.1, 9.2), composed from the published record: the support clock on the source release, the staged route (IBM's n-1 policy), what IBM says about the move (route, platform, database, Java, users, add-ons, reports; eac

tools.name: upgrade_checklist
tools.description: The phased checklist (before / during / after) for one Maximo move. Every item is CITED — its published records are resolved against the corpus on this call and an item whose records are not published is dropped — or VERIFY, a level-dependent question to settle against IBM. Optionally one phase.

tools.name: fixes_gained
tools.description: Every FIX and SECURITY record the 9.x change log holds for the releases inside a move (the 9.x log starts at 9.1). Optionally one functional area. Counted, never scored as upgrade weight.

tools.name: deprecation_register
tools.description: What was deprecated, removed or renamed in Maximo / MAS, in which version, what IBM says replaces it (blank when IBM has not named one), and the published records that say so. Curated; rows publish only on evidence. Same data as assetize.com.au/upgrade/deprecations.

tools.name: lifecycle_dates
tools.description: End-of-support, Extended Support and Dual Support dates for Maximo and MAS as structured rows: product, version, milestone, ISO date, days remaining, and the IBM page each comes from. Optionally scope by product or version. Same data as assetize.com.au/upgrade/deadlines.

tools.name: maximo_mobile
tools.description: Researched IBM statements about Maximo Mobile, by topic: what it is, the shell and Graphite-app architecture, device requirements (OS levels, memory, WebView2, ARCore, shared devices), getting the app onto devices (stores, MSIX, QR server URL, MDM), login and shared devices, data sync and attachment

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_records, get_record, change_watch, list_gotchas, maximo_mobile · Private data: ask_maximo, search_records, lookup_error_code, get_record, maximo_changelog, change_watch, list_gotchas, records_by_version, behaviour_history, support_lifecycle, corpus_stats, upgrade_plan, upgrade_checklist, fixes_gained, deprecation_register · Public sink: deprecation_register · Destructive: test_automation_script_evidence.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_records, get_record, change_watch, list_gotchas, maximo_mobile · Private data: ask_maximo, search_records, lookup_error_code, get_record, maximo_changelog, change_watch, list_gotchas, records_by_version, behaviour_history, support_lifecycle, corpus_stats, upgrade_plan, upgrade_checklist, fixes_gained, deprecation_register · Public sink: deprecation_register · Destructive: test_automation_script_evidence

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
